resources.string: Add the Float Tools home-screen widget. Defaults: tap once for play/pause, twice for rotate, three times for brightness, four times for browser tabs, or five times for Photos crop; repeat the same taps to hide. Customize each tool below. Leave less than 450 ms between taps.

Chrome and Firefox controls. Tap the circle to close a tab; drag it to move. Swipe the rectangle left/right to change tabs; drag vertically or diagonally to move. Enable tab accessibility from Permissions. Disable the separate Tab Bubble service when using this tool to avoid duplicate controls.
Shows only while Google Photos is cropping and rotating a photo. Choose the straighten drag and the photo drag below. Enable photo-crop accessibility from Permissions.
Smallest step (4 px past the touch slop)
22 px — 7a moved the photo 1 px up
25 px — 7a slide of a few pixels
Enable Float Tools — photo crop in Android Accessibility settings first.

When this tool is enabled, Float Tools reads the Google Photos crop screen and drags the straighten bar or the photo by the length chosen in Float Tools. It appears only while Crop and rotate is open. Float Tools does not save or send screen contents and has no internet permission. You can disable this service in Android Accessibility settings at any time.
Move the photo up one step
Move the photo down one step
Move the photo left one step
Move the photo right one step
Photos is not showing the crop rotation slider.
Photos is not showing the crop area to drag.
The crop rotation slider is already at its limit.
Android did not accept the crop drag. Re-enable photo-crop accessibility.
Enable Float Tools — browser tabs in Android Accessibility settings first.
Default: swipe left for next tab; right for previous tab.
Reversed: swipe left for previous tab; right for next tab.
Swipe left for next tab, right for previous tab. Drag vertically or diagonally to move the whole widget.
Swipe left for previous tab, right for next tab. Drag vertically or diagonally to move the whole widget.

When this tool is enabled, Float Tools reads native Chrome and Firefox controls and performs clicks and toolbar gestures on your behalf to close or switch tabs. Accessibility permission can expose screen contents. Float Tools does not save or send screen contents and has no internet permission. The tab widget appears only over the supported browsers. You can disable this service in Android Accessibility settings at any time.
Control the active media player from any screen.
Allow Float Tools to display over other apps to use floating buttons.
Allow Float Tools to change system settings to use Auto-rotate and Brightness.
Allow Float Tools to display over other apps, then open it again.
Shown while floating utility buttons are on screen.
Tap this notification to hide all floating tools.
Tap to toggle floating tools. Configure tap counts in Float Tools.
Long-press your home screen, choose Widgets, then Float Tools.
Each tool needs a different tap count. Change the other tool first.
No tool assigned to this tap count.
Drag to move. Double-tap and drag around the dial to adjust brightness. Tap to toggle automatic brightness. The lowest range gradually adds Extra Dim.
Brightness: %1$d%%, %2$s. Drag to move; double-tap and turn to adjust; the lowest range adds Extra Dim.
Could not change brightness. Check system settings access.
For precise play/pause icons, allow Float Tools notification access. Without it, the icon follows music audio activity.
Extra Dim control needs one-time setup through a connected computer.
